entry.title: Factorio: Space Age v2.3.0
entry.content:
# Factorio: Space Age apworld 2.3.0
* Now based on Factorio 2.1 🎉 * As of writing this, Factorio 2.1.14 itself is still experimental. Please report bugs or incompatibilities, and thanks for being an early tester of both this apworld and Factorio 2.1! * The new `stellar-discovery-solar-system-edge` technology means that the `progressive-promethium` large group has one extra item. * Moving `biter-egg` and `nutrients-from-biter-egg` recipes to `biter-egg-handling` means the `progressive-captivity` large group has one extra item. * The default number of filler nothing items is now 3 instead of 4, because `biter-egg-handling` is no longer an empty technology. * New YAML option `intermediate_technologies: unlocked` enabled by default, which unlocks 19 technologies from the start that only give intermediate products. This option doesn't give free samples for these intermediates. See https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/blob/space-age/worlds/factorio_space_age/data/ap_data.py for the list of technologies. [#37](https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/issues/37) * New YAML option `production_and_utility_science: removed` disabled by default, which allows for a smaller scale game, particularly with shorter objectives like `goal: any_other_planet_science`. * Research objectives beyond your configured goal are removed. For example, `goal: aquilo_orbit` will remove all research locations involving cryogenic science packs. When combined with `infinite_technologies: shuffle` (the default), infinite technologies beyond the goal are moved earlier instead of removed, copying the ingredients, prerequisites, and count formula of an earlier infinite technology. This can enable Factorio: Space Age players to unblock themselves by researching large progressive groups from infinite technology locations out of logic once enough science packs are unlocked, always at least chemical science. [#11](https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/issues/11) * Fix filler items not contributing to their progressive group like they're supposed to. * Improved information in the technology GUI: * Progressive chains are shown as dependencies between the inaccessible vanilla technologies, visualizing progressive chains. [#19](https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/issues/19) * Move multiworld item name from description to trigger description. Thanks @CosmicWolf/@Enderdraak for suggesting this in [#31](https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/issues/31) and [#30](https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/pull/30). * Move localizable strings to `locale/en/locale.cfg` (no longer dynamically generated), which should enable third-party translations. Thanks @CosmicWolf/@Enderdraak for the reference implementation in [#30](https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/pull/30).

entry.title: Final Fantasy Tactics Ivalice Island v0.4.0
entry.content:
# Final Fantasy Tactics APWorld Update v0.4.0
This release is not backwards compatible with previous releases.
## APWorld Changes - Changes - Move-Find Item (MFI) randomization has been added. - This setting makes MFI tiles send out multiworld locations. - This can be configured to optionally trigger MFI tiles with any Chemist or any unit on your team. - Regardless of whether the tiles are randomized to be multiworld locations, you can randomize the ingame reward given by the tile. - Ingame poach rewards can now be randomized. - The client has been changed to trigger in battle rewards automatically. - This applies to MFI tiles, poach rewards, and job unlocks. - The Transmooglifier setting has been added. - This setting changes Rad, Alicia, and Lavian to have special custom jobs designed specifically for Ivalice Island. - The pool of jobs it picks from can be customized. - Enemy Randomizer now has a `boss shuffle randomized` option which shuffles unique "boss" units among each other and randomizes all other units per your settings. - A Vanilla Changes option has been added allowing you to customize which changes from vanilla behavior you'd like enabled. - A vanilla change enabled by default has been added to adjust shop inventories. This adds an early Katana and Polearm to castle shops and adds the basic guns to trade cities. - In Enemy Randomizer, a level boost is applied to "boss" units so even when they randomize into common units they have a bit more of a punch than their hangers-on. - In Enemy Randomizer, a special template for Summoners with the Zodiac spell available has been added. - An alternate final boss battle has been added for those who wish to test their skills (or are merely bored at the end of a multiworld game). This final battle is of an increased difficulty, is not affected by Enemy Randomizer, and is never required. Clearing it, however, will win the game just as clearing the Graveyard of Airships 2 fight would. - Bugfixes - In Enemy Randomizer, Sorceror (Kletian's job) now has its primary skillset always available.
[Setup Guide](https://github.com/Rosalie-A/Archipelago/wiki/Final-Fantasy-Tactics:-Ivalice-Island-Setup-Guide)

entry.title: Librarian Tidy Up the Arcane Library v2.0.3
entry.content:
## Librarian-AP v2.0.3
Spare unlocks so you get BK'd less often, plus three fixes.
**Existing runs are unaffected.** Nothing here changes a seed in progress.
## `extra_series_percent` is now `spare_book_item_percent`
**Regenerate your YAML to update the name.** Same default of 10, but capped at 20 now.
Renamed because it does more than one job. On `goal: custom` it works as it did in 2.0.2. It now also applies to **full and floor goals**, adding that percentage of extra `Progressive Series Unlock` items to the pool, replacing filler.
A full or floor goal needs every series in its scope, so one unlock sitting in a stalled or abandoned game can leave you stuck for good. The spares mean you need most of them rather than all.
## New: `spare_shelf_items`
The same for bookcases, on full and floor goals. A count per bookcase rather than a percentage: it adds an extra N `Progressive Shelf Unlock` items for each section, replacing filler.
```yaml spare_shelf_items: 0 # 0-3, default 0 ```
It is the most expensive setting in the YAML, one item slot per bookcase per step. A seed with no room for the number you pick uses fewer and says so during generation.
Both settings are `progressive_unlocks` only, where unlock items are interchangeable.
## Fix: BookSanity with `goal: custom` could fail to generate
In 2.0.2 it could fail outright with an accessibility error listing `Reached Level` locations. The level filter used the row count you asked for, not the rows the trimmed seed holds.
## Fix: UT showing every level as reachable
In BookSanity the level checks read as in logic from the start, with sphere trackers putting all 45 in sphere 1. Levels come from finishing **rows**, but the logic counted **books**: level 45 wants 254 rows and was asked for 254 books, of 3072.
## Fix: UT modeling the wrong starting items
Universal Tracker re-runs generation without seeing your YAML, so `starting_series_count` and `series_per_unlock` came from defaults and it modeled the wrong number of starting series unlocks.
## Updating
> Extract the zip and drop `Librarian/` into your Steam install (overwrite). Drop the > included `librarian.apworld` into your Archipelago `custom_worlds/` folder. Requires > game build 1.0.12 or newer. The title screen top-right should read `LibAP v2.0.3`.
## If something breaks
Send `crash_trace.log` (the header should read `mod=2.0.3`), the last ~200 lines of `UE4SS.log`, your YAML's `Librarian:` section, and one line on what you were doing.

entry.title: Logic Test v0.3.0
entry.content:
## Sphere model fix: locked placements no longer break lock-step
Fixed the bug where locked in-game placements in the under-test game (vanilla or shuffled badges, HMs, key items) caused interleaved keys — e.g. lots of `KEY_12` arriving while `KEY_11` was still incomplete — along with false `LOGIC LEAK` warnings in the client. These items are never gated by the KEY spheres, so the player picks them up mid-sphere in real play; the sphere model now collects them via closure (like events) in both `count_events` modes, restoring the lock-step guarantee: a `KEY_(i+1)` is never legitimately reachable before every `KEY_i`.
Related hardening: - The unreachable-marker pass uses the same networkable-location predicate as the sphere computation. - Generation fails loudly if the fixed-location snapshot hook didn't run, instead of silently falling back to post-fill lock flags. - Non-advancement items are skipped in the closure sets (they can't affect reachability). - New regression test replays gated play via `MultiWorld.get_spheres` against a slot with shuffled (locked) badges/HMs.
## Client improvements
- **Leak tracking persists across reconnects**: keys received ahead of the current sphere are recorded in server data storage (per team/slot), so leak history survives reconnects and item replays. Leaked spheres are flagged in the status output and GUI with the sphere they arrived on. - **Per-sphere key totals**: the status list and GUI tab now show have/required key counts for every sphere (done / now / locked), not just the current one.
## Upgrade notes
Seeds generated with 0.2.1 or earlier keep their old (misgrouped) key assignment — the fix applies at generation time, so affected multiworlds need a regen. Existing games remain playable; the early keys are safe and the leak warnings they trigger are spurious.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.8.0r2
entry.content: Slot-filtered rewards now hand out what the multiworld actually promised. A "Unique Weapon" or "Set Helm" was quietly falling back to a random roll of any kind, because the mod looked up which equipment slot an item belongs to by reading armor.txt and weapons.txt from the game folder — and those files have not shipped since 3.7.6, when they were removed for being Blizzard's own. The engine never noticed, since it reads them from your game archives; our own code could not. The table is now built into the mod, so it cannot go missing again, and a modded install that carries its own tables still overrides it.

entry.title: OpenTTD v1.4.1r3
entry.content: Started from the launcher, the game now goes straight in: no start dialog, no fields to fill. It loads this seed's own savegame when one exists and generates the world when none does; quitting — and every autosave — writes that per-seed save, so the next press of Play continues where you left off. Each seed keeps its own save, so two seeds can never pick up each other's progress. Requires plugin 1.2.1 (included).

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.8.7
entry.content:
The Sorceress no longer crashes her way into the game. Diablo II would stop with its own assertion box — SCmd.cpp, line 3910 — within seconds of reaching town, and only for her; every other class played fine. At startup the mod rewrote the skill animations of all seven classes at once, before it knew which class was about to be played, and then put the player's own skills back to normal a moment later when the character loaded. Three Sorceress skills carry the animations that were being rewritten, and changing them under the game's feet threw off the queue Diablo II keeps of commands it has sent and is still waiting to hear back about. Animations are now applied once, per class, when the character loads, so nothing is ever written and then taken back. Every class keeps its own animations, and a skill borrowed from another class still falls back to an attack animation exactly as before.
Version numbers agree with each other again. The bootstrap launcher was still reporting 3.8.3 and the packaged Archipelago world still declared 3.8.3, four releases after the rest of the mod had moved on.

entry.title: Diablo II Archipelago v3.8.8
entry.content:
The startup crash is fixed. Diablo II would stop with its own assertion box — SCmd.cpp line 3910 — seconds after a character entered town, sometimes on the first try and sometimes after a dozen, on any class. The mod sent its internal packets to the wrong address: what it called D2Client's send function is in fact D2Client's weapon-swap command handler, and calling it left a register the handler reads holding whatever happened to be there. Depending on that value the game carried on, raised the assertion box, or faulted outright, which is why the crash came and went with no pattern. Packets now go through D2Net's real send function, the one the rest of the mod already used.
Bow, crossbow and javelin skills keep their weapon requirement. It was being stripped along with every other weapon restriction, so a character who was dealt Fire Arrow among the random starting skills could select and cast it while holding a staff. The requirement is what makes Diablo II refuse the cast until a bow is equipped, and the skills stay in the pool for every class — anyone can pick up a bow and use them.
Crash reports name the module behind every stack address, and every skill change on either hand is logged with the item that granted it. Both are there so a report from a player carries what is needed to place a fault without a second round of questions.

Setup Guide with installation instructions and additional information for PsychoRando here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1b7QOnOLmTSvdC7A1YK3bsSmhtSOsAMs0XF5j-tyE6Zw/edit?usp=sharing
Requires Astralathe to run, download and installation instructions found here: https://gitlab.com/scrunguscrungus/astralathe/-/wikis/Installing%20Astralathe
PopTracker Pack created by Mysteryem here: https://github.com/Mysteryem/Psychonauts_AP_PopTracker/releases
# Psychonauts Archipelago Setup Guide
## Setting up the required mods 1. Install Psychonauts for PC, Astralathe, and the Psychonauts Randomizer Mod from the AP Companion Branch. Full Psychonauts Randomizer and Astralathe setup guide here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1b7QOnOLmTSvdC7A1YK3bsSmhtSOsAMs0XF5j-tyE6Zw/edit?usp=sharing **Make sure Astralathe is up to date, use the AP Companion Branch of PsychoRando, and make sure to open the game with AstralatheLauncher.exe at least once.**
2. Download the psychonauts.apworld and install (easiest method is by trying to open the apworld file, Archipelago will install automatically)
3. Open the Archipelago Launcher and run the Psychonauts Client. If you get an error message saying the root_directory could not be found, follow steps 4-5. Otherwise, skip to step 6.
4. Find the folder that contains your Psychonauts and Astralathe installation, and copy the folder directory. For example, the most common place for the Steam version is "C:\\\\Program Files (x86)\\\\Steam\\\\steamapps\\\\common\\\\Psychonauts"
5. Run ArchipelagoLauncher.exe and open host.yaml from the Archipelago Launcher, find the psychonauts_options and paste your psychonauts game directory into the root_directory setting between the quotes. **If the root directory contains single slashes between lines, change all of these to double slashes. If you don't, the client will fail to open**
6. Click "Generate Template Settings". This will open file explorer Find "Psychonauts.yaml" and copy it to /Players/ (create this folder if it does not exist)
7. Open the YAML file and change the line that says "name: Player{number}" to your desired player name. Adjust the settings in the YAML to your liking
8. Run ArchipelagoGenerate.exe
9. Take the newly created AP_XXX.zip file in /output/ in upload it here: https://archipelago.gg/uploads then create a room
10. Download patch file next to your player name, then unzip the file. This contains a file called RandoSeed.lua
11. Find your Psychonauts game directory and open /ModResource/PsychoRando/Scripts
12. Paste RandoSeed.lua from your generated Archipelago file into this folder. Replace the file in the destination if needed.
13. Run AstralatheLauncher.exe to open the game. You should see your player number and name on the menu screen, along with your current randomizer version.
14. From the menu, enter the yellow door to start a new game.
15. From the Archipelago Launcher, open the Psychonauts Client and connect to your server hosted on archipelago.gg
16. Once you've started a new save file and connected to the server, you can start playing!

If the intro is skipped then you will be prompted to select your starter Pokémon during Oak's initial speech - This setting is forced on if Random Starting Town or any type of Entrance Randomization is on - Updated option `shuffle_pokemon_centers` - Now includes the Player's House though your starting town's Pokémon Center entrance will never lead there - Updated option `mix_entrance_warp_pools` - Added `Pokemon Centers` as an option - Your starting town's Pokémon Center entrance is guaranteed to lead to a Pokémon Center - Added `Warp Tiles` as an option - Warp Tiles will only be mixed if using `full` Warp Tiles shuffle - Added `Dropdowns` as an option - Dropdowns will only be mixed is using `full` Dropdown shuffle and entrances/warps are decoupled - Updated option `prizesanity` - The coin price for purchasing items at the Game Corner Prize Room will now be determined by what item it is - Updated option `shop_prices` and `consistent_shop_prices` - Now applies to Game Corner Prize Room item purchases as well - Updated option `trainersanity` - Split into `kanto_trainersanity` and `sevii_trainersanity` options - New option `item_appearance_matches_contents` - Changes the color of item balls to match their contents.
